newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banks downplay Moody's downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Thai banks downplay Moody's downgrades.

text.p: Major Thai banks on Wednesday played down a decision by Moody's Investors Service to downgrade their senior debt and deposit ratings, saying it would have little immediate impact on their foreign funding costs.
Moody's lowered the ratings of Bangkok Bank Plc, Thai Farmers Bank Plc, Siam Commercial Bank Plc, Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand, and Export-Import Bank of Thailand, to A3 from A2.
Piti Sithi-amnuay, vice chairman of Bangkok Bank, told reporters the downgrade would probably raise his bank's future funding cost by two to five basis points.
He said the Thai bank downgrades were mandatory and in line with Moody's cut of Thailand's long-term foreign currency ceilings for bonds, also to A3 from A2.
Piti said Moody's was expected to review Thai ratings in June when they could be improved if the Thai economy showed signs of recovery.

Somchai Sanyasiri of Siam Commercial Bank told Reuters the market had discounted the Moody's action before its announcement which should not produce any short-term negative impact on general funding costs of Thai banks.
"There was virtually no market reaction. The funding cost of each Thai bank will be up to individual credit standing. If there is any impact, it should be on long-term bonds," he said.
Som Pisarnsopon, vice president of Thai Farmers Bank, said the bank downgrades were partly a product of a slowing Thai economy and its related problems.

The prices of the banks hit by the downgrade fell slightly on the Thai bourse. Bangkok Bank fell three baht to 187 baht, Thai Farmers bank fell one baht to 122 and Siam Commercial was unchanged at 137 baht.
